claim: TACAN was recently reported as a mechanosensitive ion channel.
source: A mechanosensitive ion channel called TACAN was recently reported.
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature reporting TACAN as a mechanosensitive ion channel

claim: TACAN did not produce pressure-evoked currents in CHO cells expressing TACAN.
source: Using CHO cells, similar to those used in the original study, we did not observe pressure-evoked currents in excised membrane patches (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by experimental patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1A,B

claim: Background channels that were not sensitive to pressure steps were observed in CHO cells expressing either TACAN or the M2 muscarinic receptor as a control.
source: Background channels that were not sensitive to the pressure steps were observed in CHO cells expressing either TACAN or the M2 muscarinic receptor as a control.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations from patch-clamp recordings

claim: TACAN expressed in a Piezo1 knockout HEK cell line did not elicit pressure-activated channels.
source: Similarly, TACAN expressed in a Piezo1 knockout HEK cell line did not elicit pressure-activated channels (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1C,D

claim: Purified TACAN protein reconstituted into giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs) did not yield pressure-activated channels.
source: Purified TACAN protein reconstituted into giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs) of soy L-α-phosphatidylcholine (soy-PC) also did not yield pressure-activated channels in membrane patches isolated from the GUVs (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental patch-clamp recordings from GUVs shown in Figure 1E

claim: Mechanosensitive TRAAK channels have been successfully recorded in GUVs using the identical approach.
source: We note that previously we have successfully recorded mechanosensitive TRAAK channels in GUVs using the identical approach (Brohawn et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work from the same laboratory

claim: When TACAN was reconstituted at high protein-to-lipid ratios (≥1:100, m:m), transient currents were observed.
source: When TACAN was expressed, purified, and reconstituted into both GUVs and planar lipid bilayers at high protein-to-lipid ratios (≥1:100, m:m), transient currents were observed, as shown in Figure 2.
evidence: Supported by experimental recordings shown in Figure 2

claim: The transient currents observed at high TACAN concentrations were insensitive to pressure.
source: These currents were insensitive to pressure applied to patches isolated from the GUVs (Figure 1E) and heterogeneous in amplitude (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental recordings shown in Figures 1E and 2A-C

claim: The transient currents observed at high TACAN concentrations were heterogeneous in amplitude.
source: These currents were insensitive to pressure applied to patches isolated from the GUVs (Figure 1E) and heterogeneous in amplitude (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental recordings shown in Figure 2A-C

claim: The properties of currents observed at high TACAN concentrations do not resemble aspects of currents from known ion channels.
source: These properties do not resemble aspects of currents from known ion channels but might suggest that TACAN renders the membrane transiently leaky when reconstituted at high protein concentrations.
evidence: Based on comparison of observed current properties with known ion channel properties

claim: TACAN might render the membrane transiently leaky when reconstituted at high protein concentrations.
source: These properties do not resemble aspects of currents from known ion channels but might suggest that TACAN renders the membrane transiently leaky when reconstituted at high protein concentrations.
evidence: Speculative interpretation based on observed heterogeneous current properties

claim: The structure of TACAN was determined at 3.5 Å resolution using single-particle cryo-EM.
source: Alongside the functional characterization, we analyzed the structure of TACAN determined at 3.5 Å resolution using single-particle cryo-EM.
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM data collection and processing described in Materials and methods

claim: TACAN is an α-helical transmembrane protein that forms a symmetric dimer.
source: TACAN is an α-helical TM protein that forms a symmetric dimer (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3A

claim: Each TACAN protomer consists of six transmembrane helices (S1–S6).
source: Each protomer consists of six TM helices (S1–S6), which form a barrel surrounding a tunnel open to the cytoplasm (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3C

claim: The six transmembrane helices in TACAN form a barrel surrounding a tunnel open to the cytoplasm.
source: Each protomer consists of six TM helices (S1–S6), which form a barrel surrounding a tunnel open to the cytoplasm (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3C

claim: Non-continuous density was observed inside the tunnel of TACAN, suggesting the presence of a small, non-protein molecule.
source: Non-continuous density was observed inside the tunnel, suggesting the presence of a small, non-protein molecule (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM density map shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A

claim: The two protomers of the TACAN dimer bury an extensive surface area of 3049 Å2.
source: The two protomers of the TACAN dimer bury an extensive surface area of 3049 Å2, mediated through the TM domain as well as two long N-terminal helices that form a coiled coil (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Supported by structural analysis of the cryo-EM structure

claim: The dimer interface in TACAN is mediated through the transmembrane domain as well as two long N-terminal helices that form a coiled coil.
source: The two protomers of the TACAN dimer bury an extensive surface area of 3049 Å2, mediated through the TM domain as well as two long N-terminal helices that form a coiled coil (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B

claim: The DALI three-dimensional structure comparison server identified ELOVL7 as a homologous protein to TACAN.
source: The DALI three-dimensional structure comparison server (Holm and Rosenström, 2010) identified a homologous protein called ELOVL7, a long-chain fatty acid (FA) elongase (Figure 4; Nie et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by computational structure comparison using DALI server

claim: ELOVL7 is a long-chain fatty acid elongase.
source: The DALI three-dimensional structure comparison server (Holm and Rosenström, 2010) identified a homologous protein called ELOVL7, a long-chain fatty acid (FA) elongase (Figure 4; Nie et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature on ELOVL7

claim: ELOVL7 catalyzes the first step in the fatty acid elongation cycle by transferring an acetyl group from malonyl-CoA onto long-chain FA-CoA.
source: This enzyme catalyzes the first step in the FA elongation cycle by transferring an acetyl group from malonyl-CoA onto long-chain FA-CoA (Naganuma et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature on ELOVL7 enzymatic activity

claim: The transmembrane domain in TACAN is similar to ELOVL7.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, the TM domain in TACAN is indeed similar to ELOVL7.
evidence: Supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 4A

claim: The tunnel in ELOVL7 is lined by catalytically important histidine residues.
source: The tunnel in ELOVL7 is lined by catalytically important histidine residues and contains a covalently linked eicosanoyl-CoA molecule (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: Supported by structural analysis of ELOVL7 shown in Figure 4B,C

claim: The tunnel in ELOVL7 contains a covalently linked eicosanoyl-CoA molecule.
source: The tunnel in ELOVL7 is lined by catalytically important histidine residues and contains a covalently linked eicosanoyl-CoA molecule (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: Supported by structural analysis of ELOVL7 shown in Figure 4B,C

claim: TACAN conserves two of the four histidine residues found in ELOVL7.
source: TACAN conserves two of the four histidine residues (Figure 4B,D).
evidence: Supported by sequence alignment and structural comparison shown in Figure 4B,D

claim: The structure of TACAN with His196 and His197 mutated to alanine was determined at 2.8 Å resolution.
source: To determine the identity of the small molecule implied by the broken density in the tunnel of TACAN (Figure 4E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3A), we determined the structure of TACAN with His196 and His197 mutated to alanine at 2.8 Å resolution (Table 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM data collection and processing described in Materials and methods and Table 1

claim: The map of TACAN His196Ala His197Ala mutant showed clearer density consistent with a coenzyme A molecule (CoASH).
source: The map showed clearer density consistent with a coenzyme A molecule (CoASH) (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM density map shown in Figure 4F

claim: Native mass spectrometry was used to confirm the identity of the cofactor as CoASH.
source: Native mass spectrometry (nMS) was used to confirm the identity as CoASH (Figure 5).
evidence: Supported by native mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5

claim: The purified TACAN His196Ala His197Ala sample contains a mixture of the 83,237 Da, +767 Da, and +1535 Da mass species, corresponding to an apo form, one and two CoASH bound forms, respectively.
source: As shown in Figure 5B, the purified TACANH196A H197A sample contains a mixture of the 83,237 Da, +767 Da, and +1535 Da mass species, corresponding to an apo form, one and two CoASH bound forms, respectively.
evidence: Supported by native mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5B

claim: After incubation with CoASH, some fraction of the apo form of TACAN His196Ala His197Ala shifts to one and two CoASH bound forms.
source: After incubation with CoASH, some fraction of the apo form shifts to one and two CoASH bound forms.
evidence: Supported by native mass spectrometry data

claim: The +767 Da and +1535 Da species in TACAN His196Ala His197Ala are replaced by +795 Da and +1591 Da or +811 Da and +1622 Da species after incubation with S-ethyl-CoA or Acetyl-CoA, corresponding to the CoASH analogue bound forms.
source: Additionally, the +767 Da and +1535 Da species are replaced by +795 Da and +1591 Da or +811 Da and +1622 Da species after incubation with the two CoASH analogues S-ethyl-CoA or Acetyl-CoA, corresponding to the CoASH analogue bound forms.
evidence: Supported by native mass spectrometry data

claim: In the purified TACAN wild-type sample, the apo form is dominant.
source: In the purified TACANWT sample, the apo form is dominant and incubation with S-ethyl-CoA shifts it to one and two analogue bound forms (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by native mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5A

claim: Incubation of TACAN wild-type with S-ethyl-CoA shifts the apo form to one and two analogue bound forms.
source: In the purified TACANWT sample, the apo form is dominant and incubation with S-ethyl-CoA shifts it to one and two analogue bound forms (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by native mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5A

claim: TACAN is co-purified with endogenous coenzyme A.
source: Together, these data are consistent with our cryo-EM results and indicate that TACAN is co-purified with endogenous coenzyme A.
evidence: Inferred from combined cryo-EM and native mass spectrometry data

claim: CoASH binds with different conformations in TACAN from ELOVL7.
source: It is noteworthy that CoASH binds with different conformations in TACAN from ELOVL7 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B; Nie et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B

claim: No enzymatic activity was observed for TACAN using a free-CoA detection assay.
source: In addition, no enzymatic activity was observed for TACAN using a free-CoA detection assay (for details, see Materials and methods), which demonstrated robust activity for ELOVL7 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), thus TACAN does not appear to catalyze the same reaction as ELOVL7.
evidence: Supported by enzymatic assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C

claim: The free-CoA detection assay demonstrated robust activity for ELOVL7.
source: In addition, no enzymatic activity was observed for TACAN using a free-CoA detection assay (for details, see Materials and methods), which demonstrated robust activity for ELOVL7 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), thus TACAN does not appear to catalyze the same reaction as ELOVL7.
evidence: Supported by enzymatic assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C

claim: TACAN does not appear to catalyze the same reaction as ELOVL7.
source: In addition, no enzymatic activity was observed for TACAN using a free-CoA detection assay (for details, see Materials and methods), which demonstrated robust activity for ELOVL7 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), thus TACAN does not appear to catalyze the same reaction as ELOVL7.
evidence: Inferred from lack of enzymatic activity in the assay that works for ELOVL7

claim: If TACAN is a coenzyme A-dependent enzyme, its substrate is unknown.
source: If TACAN is a coenzyme A-dependent enzyme, its substrate is unknown.
evidence: Speculative statement based on lack of enzymatic activity with tested substrates

claim: The authors were unable to replicate evidence of mechanosensitive channel activity for TACAN.
source: We undertook this study to understand how TACAN functions as an MSC, but have been unable to replicate evidence of MSC activity.
evidence: Summary statement based on all electrophysiological experiments performed

claim: No channel activity was observed in the plasma membrane of cells expressing TACAN.
source: We observe no channel activity in the plasma membrane of cells expressing TACAN and the heterogeneous-in-amplitude currents (without mechanosensitive properties) that we observe when we reconstitute TACAN at high protein concentrations are not consistent with other native biological channels that we have studied.
evidence: Supported by patch-clamp recordings from cells expressing TACAN

claim: The heterogeneous-in-amplitude currents observed when TACAN is reconstituted at high protein concentrations are not consistent with other native biological channels that the authors have studied.
source: We observe no channel activity in the plasma membrane of cells expressing TACAN and the heterogeneous-in-amplitude currents (without mechanosensitive properties) that we observe when we reconstitute TACAN at high protein concentrations are not consistent with other native biological channels that we have studied.
evidence: Based on comparison with the authors' experience with other ion channels

claim: TACAN is structurally related to coenzyme A-dependent fatty acid elongases.
source: Structurally, TACAN is related to coenzyme A-dependent FA elongases; however, without further data we cannot conclude that TACAN itself functions as an enzyme.
evidence: Supported by structural comparison with ELOVL7

claim: Without further data, the authors cannot conclude that TACAN itself functions as an enzyme.
source: Structurally, TACAN is related to coenzyme A-dependent FA elongases; however, without further data we cannot conclude that TACAN itself functions as an enzyme.
evidence: Cautious interpretation based on structural similarity but lack of enzymatic activity

claim: It remains to be determined which membranes in a cell express TACAN.
source: It also remains to be determined which membranes in a cell express TACAN.
evidence: Statement of unknown information

claim: The authors do not find evidence that TACAN is a mechanosensitive ion channel.
source: In conclusion, we do not find evidence that TACAN is a mechanosensitive ion channel.
evidence: Summary conclusion based on all experimental data

claim: The strength of the conclusion that TACAN is not a mechanosensitive ion channel is in the electrophysiological interrogation.
source: The strength of this conclusion is in the electrophysiological interrogation.
evidence: Meta-statement about the weight of different types of evidence

claim: The structure of TACAN, because it looks like a known enzyme, is compatible with the 'not a channel' conclusion, but the structure alone would not make a strong argument.
source: The structure, because it looks like a known enzyme, is compatible with the 'not a channel' conclusion, but the structure alone would not make a strong argument.
evidence: Meta-statement about the weight of structural evidence

claim: A number of ion channels, including CLC channels, TMEM16, and CFTR, are not obviously ion channels based on their structures.
source: A number of ion channels, including CLC channels (Dutzler et al., 2002; Dutzler et al., 2003; Feng et al., 2012; Park et al., 2017; Park and MacKinnon, 2018), TMEM16 (Dang et al., 2017; Paulino et al., 2017), and CFTR (Liu et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2018), are not obviously ion channels based on their structures and indeed each are fairly indistinguishable from proteins exhibiting non-channel functions.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior structural studies of ion channels

claim: CLC channels, TMEM16, and CFTR are each fairly indistinguishable from proteins exhibiting non-channel functions based on their structures.
source: A number of ion channels, including CLC channels (Dutzler et al., 2002; Dutzler et al., 2003; Feng et al., 2012; Park et al., 2017; Park and MacKinnon, 2018), TMEM16 (Dang et al., 2017; Paulino et al., 2017), and CFTR (Liu et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2018), are not obviously ion channels based on their structures and indeed each are fairly indistinguishable from proteins exhibiting non-channel functions.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior structural studies

claim: TACAN was originally identified in a proteomics screen and called TMEM120A.
source: TACAN, originally identified in a proteomics screen and called TMEM120A, was categorized as a nuclear envelope protein (NET29) that participates in lipid metabolism (Batrakou et al., 2015; Byerly et al., 2010; Haakonsson et al., 2013; Lee et al., 2005; Rosell et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature

claim: TACAN was categorized as a nuclear envelope protein (NET29) that participates in lipid metabolism.
source: TACAN, originally identified in a proteomics screen and called TMEM120A, was categorized as a nuclear envelope protein (NET29) that participates in lipid metabolism (Batrakou et al., 2015; Byerly et al., 2010; Haakonsson et al., 2013; Lee et al., 2005; Rosell et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature

claim: Adipocyte-specific TMEM120A knockout mice exhibited a lipodystrophy syndrome similar to human familial partial lipodystrophy FPLD2.
source: Adipocyte-specific TMEM120A knockout mice exhibited a lipodystrophy syndrome similar to human familial partial lipodystrophy FPLD2 (Czapiewski et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature

claim: TACAN was proposed to mediate mechanical pain.
source: Recently, a new MSC in mammals called TACAN was reported and proposed to mediate mechanical pain (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature

claim: Mechanosensitive ion channels open in response to mechanical forces.
source: Mechanosensitive ion channels (MSCs) open in response to mechanical forces (Guharay and Sachs, 1984; Guharay and Sachs, 1985; Kung, 2005; Sachs, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature establishing this fundamental property

claim: When mechanosensitive ion channels open, ions flow across the cell membrane, triggering subsequent biochemical processes.
source: When the channels open, ions flow across the cell membrane, triggering subsequent biochemical processes that ultimately represent a cellular response to the applied mechanical force.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of ion channel function

claim: The coupling of transmembrane ion flow to mechanical forces underlies some forms of osmoregulation, cell and organ growth, blood pressure regulation, touch, and hearing.
source: This coupling of transmembrane (TM) ion flow to mechanical forces underlies some forms of osmoregulation, cell and organ growth, blood pressure regulation, touch, and hearing (Chalfie, 2009; Coste et al., 2010; Pan et al., 2013; Peyronnet et al., 2012; Woo et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature

claim: Several mechanosensitive ion channels have been discovered and characterized.
source: Several MSCs have been discovered and characterized (Kefauver et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature

claim: The orientation of TACAN with respect to the cytoplasm is unknown.
source: The orientation of the protein with respect to the cytoplasm is unknown; however, the charge distribution on TACAN (von Heijne, 1986) as well as the possible presence of an enzyme active site exposed to the cytoplasm (discussed below) suggests the orientation shown (Figure 3B).
evidence: Statement of uncertainty about membrane orientation

claim: The charge distribution on TACAN as well as the possible presence of an enzyme active site exposed to the cytoplasm suggests a particular orientation.
source: The orientation of the protein with respect to the cytoplasm is unknown; however, the charge distribution on TACAN (von Heijne, 1986) as well as the possible presence of an enzyme active site exposed to the cytoplasm (discussed below) suggests the orientation shown (Figure 3B).
evidence: Inferred from charge distribution analysis and structural features

claim: The final model for TACAN wild-type contains residues 9–72, 76-250 and 262–335.
source: Several iterative cycles of refinement using the phenix.real_space_refine with secondary structure and NCS restraints and manual adjustments in COOT yielded the final model for the TACANWT containing residues 9–72, 76-250 and 262–335 (Adams et al., 2010; Emsley et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by model building and refinement process

claim: The final model for TACAN His196Ala His197Ala contains residues 9–72, 76–250 and 262–335 as well as 2 CoASH molecules bound.
source: The final model for TACANH196A H197A contained residues 9–72, 76–250 and 262–335 as well as 2 CoASH molecules bound.
evidence: Supported by model building and refinement process

claim: The expected mass for TACAN wild-type monomer is 41,770 Da.
source: From their primary sequences, the expected masses for the proteins are TACANWT monomer: 41,770 Da, TACANWT dimer: 83,539 Da, TACANH196A H197A monomer: 41,637 Da, and TACANH196A H197A dimer: 83,275 Da.
evidence: Calculated from primary sequence

claim: The expected mass for TACAN wild-type dimer is 83,539 Da.
source: From their primary sequences, the expected masses for the proteins are TACANWT monomer: 41,770 Da, TACANWT dimer: 83,539 Da, TACANH196A H197A monomer: 41,637 Da, and TACANH196A H197A dimer: 83,275 Da.
evidence: Calculated from primary sequence

claim: The expected mass for TACAN His196Ala His197Ala monomer is 41,637 Da.
source: From their primary sequences, the expected masses for the proteins are TACANWT monomer: 41,770 Da, TACANWT dimer: 83,539 Da, TACANH196A H197A monomer: 41,637 Da, and TACANH196A H197A dimer: 83,275 Da.
evidence: Calculated from primary sequence

claim: The expected mass for TACAN His196Ala His197Ala dimer is 83,275 Da.
source: From their primary sequences, the expected masses for the proteins are TACANWT monomer: 41,770 Da, TACANWT dimer: 83,539 Da, TACANH196A H197A monomer: 41,637 Da, and TACANH196A H197A dimer: 83,275 Da.
evidence: Calculated from primary sequence

claim: CHO cells have low endogenous mechanosensitive currents.
source: CHO-K1 cells (ATCC) and piezo-1 knockout HEK-293T cells (established in this lab) were used for electrophysiology experiments because they have low endogenous mechanosensitive currents (Brohawn et al., 2014; del Marmol, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature

claim: Piezo-1 knockout HEK-293T cells have low endogenous mechanosensitive currents.
source: CHO-K1 cells (ATCC) and piezo-1 knockout HEK-293T cells (established in this lab) were used for electrophysiology experiments because they have low endogenous mechanosensitive currents (Brohawn et al., 2014; del Marmol, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior literature

claim: TACAN was observed to be a symmetrical dimeric transmembrane protein.
source: We determined the structure of TACAN using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy and observed that it is a symmetrical dimeric transmembrane protein.
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM structure determination

claim: Each TACAN protomer contains an intracellular-facing cleft with a coenzyme A cofactor.
source: Each protomer contains an intracellular-facing cleft with a coenzyme A cofactor, confirmed by mass spectrometry.
evidence: Supported by cryo-EM structure and mass spectrometry data

claim: The TACAN protomer is related in three-dimensional structure to a fatty acid elongase, ELOVL7.
source: The TACAN protomer is related in three-dimensional structure to a fatty acid elongase, ELOVL7.
evidence: Supported by structural comparison using DALI server

claim: The physiological function of TACAN remains unclear.
source: Whilst its physiological function remains unclear, we anticipate that TACAN is not a mechanosensitive ion channel.
evidence: Statement of uncertainty about function

claim: The authors anticipate that TACAN is not a mechanosensitive ion channel.
source: Whilst its physiological function remains unclear, we anticipate that TACAN is not a mechanosensitive ion channel.
evidence: Conclusion based on all experimental evidence presented

claim: TACAN, at high protein concentrations, produces heterogeneous conduction levels that are not mechanosensitive.
source: Using membrane reconstitution methods, we found that TACAN, at high protein concentrations, produces heterogeneous conduction levels that are not mechanosensitive and are most consistent with disruptions of the lipid bilayer.
evidence: Supported by reconstitution experiments in GUVs and planar lipid bilayers

claim: The heterogeneous conduction levels produced by TACAN at high protein concentrations are most consistent with disruptions of the lipid bilayer.
source: Using membrane reconstitution methods, we found that TACAN, at high protein concentrations, produces heterogeneous conduction levels that are not mechanosensitive and are most consistent with disruptions of the lipid bilayer.
evidence: Interpretation based on the properties of observed currents
